# [TASK] Bound the ai-service request parameters that size downstream work

## Task

Two request parameters that size downstream work carry no upper bound.

**`k` on `GET /api/v1/ai/search/semantic`** has no `@Min`/`@Max` and flows straight into the native query's `LIMIT`. A negative value produces `LIMIT -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects outright — the resulting `PersistenceException` surfaces as a 500. A very large value degrades the HNSW index scan toward a full sort of `user_taste_profiles` and serialises a correspondingly large result set in one response. `AiController` also lacks `@Validated`, so constraints added to the parameter would not be enforced even once written.

**`count` on the recommendations endpoint** is only floored, never capped — `countOrDefault()` returns `10` for null or non-positive input and otherwise returns the value as-is. It is then multiplied by 3 and passed to `MovieCatalogClient.fetchCandidates` as a page size, so a large `count` turns one request to ai-service into a correspondingly large page request against **movie-service**. At the top of the int range the multiplication also overflows to a negative number. Both transports reach this: REST via the unbounded `Integer` field, gRPC via the proto's `int32 count`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `k` is constrained to a sane range and the constraint is actually enforced (controller-level validation is wired up)
- [x] `count` is clamped to a documented maximum in `countOrDefault()`, so no caller can size the movie-service page request arbitrarily
- [x] The `count * 3` candidate-pool calculation cannot overflow for any accepted `count`
- [x] Out-of-range values on either parameter return 400, not 500 and not a large successful response
- [x] Tests cover the boundary and out-of-range cases on both transports

## Estimate

**Hours:** 4
